newsitem.title: UK: Seascope delays float, cites weak secondary market.
newsitem.headline: Seascope delays float, cites weak secondary market.

text.p: Seascope Shipping Holdings Plc said on Wednesday it had delayed its planned summer London Stock Exchange flotation, blaming current weakness in the smaller companies secondary market for the postponement.
The UK tanker broker said it had received a positive response to the float's marketing process but was concerned about the possibility of a volatile share price after flotation.

Chairman and chief executive Tom Young said: "It is important that the listing takes place at the right time for us and for our new shareholders, and we think this is now likely to be later this year."
Seascope had hoped to raise around four million stg via a placing which would valued the group at about 15 million stg.
The postponement comes at a time when shares in smaller companies have lagged behind larger company stocks.
Since the beginning of January 1997 the FT SmallCap Index has underperformed the FT All-share index and FTSE 100 index by around 13 percent and 17 percent respectively.

Market observers said one reason for this underperformance was investors have tended to concentrate on larger stocks with predictable earnings, avoiding smaller issues with earnings that were more cyclical.
Analysts added the current summer holiday season in London was likely to dampen investor appetite for new issues in smaller companies.
